overview.summary: The canary_pyt extension provides the reference Python-based job definition format for Canary, commonly written as .pyt files.

minimal_pattern: Place canary_pyt or canary directives at module scope.
Place executable test logic in functions.
Exit with 0 for success or raise/use Canary failure helpers for structured outcomes.

directives.summary: Directives are generation-time declarations captured by the .pyt loader and converted into JobSpecIR objects.

common.testname: Set one or more generated test families.
common.name: Alias for testname.
common.parameterize: Generate job variants from parameter values.
common.cpus: Set fixed CPU requirement without creating a named parameter variant.
common.gpus: Set fixed GPU requirement without creating a named parameter variant.
common.nodes: Set fixed node requirement without creating a named parameter variant.
common.depends_on: Declare dependencies by name, pattern, or DependencySelector-like dictionary.
common.copy: Copy source files or directories into the job workspace.
common.link: Symlink source files or directories into the job workspace.
common.sources: Declare source files without staging them.
common.exclusive: Prevent concurrent execution with other jobs.
common.load_module: Load an environment module before execution.
common.source: Source an rc file before execution.
common.set_id: Set a stable explicit ID or ID template.
common.enable: Enable or disable generated jobs conditionally.
common.skipif: Skip jobs conditionally with a reason.
common.generate_composite_base_case: Create an analysis/composite job depending on parameterized jobs.

parameters.summary: parameterize() creates named job variants. cpus(), gpus(), and nodes() set fixed resource requirements without changing the generated display name.
common_mistakes: Using cpus() when named variants such as cpus=8 are desired; use parameterize('cpus', ...) instead.
Duplicating a key between parameters and meta_parameters.
Expecting top-level runtime code to be ignored during scan unless it is guarded.

dependencies.summary: depends_on() supports strings, dictionaries, lists, and DependencySelector objects.

dictionary_keys.when: Dependency condition such as on_success, on_failure, always, or an outcome expression.
dictionary_keys.expects: Expected match count: '+', '?', '*', or a positive integer.
